body.p: TME and MKTME capability is exposed to BIOS and OS via the MSRs described in this section. Please refer to the Processor External Design Specifications for more details. The maximum number of keys available in the processor for MKTME are enumerated. BIOS activates this capability via an MSR and it must select the number of keys to be supported for MKTME during the early boot stage. Upon activation, all memory (except in the TME Exclusion range) attached to the SOC is encrypted using the AES-XTS ephemeral key (KeyID 0) that is generated by the CPU on every boot. KeyID 0 is also called the platform key.

section.title: TME Enumeration
section.p: CPUID.TME (CPUID.7.0.ECX.13) enumerates the existence of the 4 (architectural) MSRs and their MSR addresses:
Each single invocation of any of the TME MSRs is applied by Microcode to all instances of the MKTME engines in the SOC. It is not necessary to call a TME MSR once for each MKTME engine.

section.title: MKTME Enumeration
section.p: MKTME is enumerated using a separate bit in CPUID and is configured using IA32_TME_CAPABILITY and IA32_TME_ACTIVATE MSRs. MKTME requires TME and therefore, cannot be enabled without enabling TME.

table.title: IA32_TME_ACTIVATE WRMSR Response and Error Handling

row.entry: TME disabled, MSR locked subsequent RDMSR returns [BIT1:0] = '01b"

TME enabled and MSR locked subsequent RDMSR returns [BIT1:0] = '11b"
WRMSR with enabled=1 and key select=0; RNG fail
WRMSR with enabled=1 and key select=1; Non zero key restored from CPU
TME enabled and MSR locked subsequent RDMSR returns [BIT1 :0]= '11b'
WRMSR with enabled=1 and key select=1; Fail - Zero key restored from CPU
WRMSR with any other legal values
Subsequent RDMSR returns written values + lock status=1
If MK_TME_KEYID_BITS > 0 && (TME) Enable == 0 (TME must be enabled at the same point as MK-TME)
If MK_TME_KEYID_BITS > 0 and TME is not successfully activated (lock is not set)
If MK_TME_CRYPTO_ALGS reserved bits are set
